title: Browser AI Extensions — AI on Every Page

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

Browser AI extensions put AI into the right-click menu, text selection, and sidebar of any webpage — so you can summarize, explain, translate, rewrite, and ask questions without switching to a separate tab. This lesson covers the best options for Chrome and Edge, how to set them up, and the most useful things you can do with them.

## Why Browser AI Extensions Matter

Most AI use starts with opening a new tab and navigating to Claude.ai or ChatGPT. Browser extensions eliminate that friction. You're reading an article, right-click, and ask *"Summarize this in 3 sentences"* — without leaving the page.

For office workers, the typical high-value uses are:
- Summarize long articles or reports before reading them in full
- Explain technical or legal language on any page
- Translate content from other languages
- Improve email drafts in Outlook Web, Gmail, or any web form
- Ask questions about the content of any page you're viewing
- Generate responses to messages directly inside LinkedIn, Twitter, or web email

## Microsoft Edge — Built-In Copilot Sidebar (Free, No Install)

If you use Microsoft Edge, you already have a free AI sidebar. No extension needed.

**How to open it:**
- Press `Ctrl+Shift+.` (period) or click the Copilot icon (top-right of Edge toolbar)
- Or press `Ctrl+Shift+Period` on any page

**What you can do:**

*Summarize the current page:* Open the Copilot sidebar → it detects the page you're on → click **Summarize page** or type *"Summarize this article."*

*Ask questions about the page:* Type *"What are the main risks mentioned in this document?"* or *"Does this article mention a study from 2024?"*

*Compose in any text box:* Click inside any text field on any website → a small Copilot compose icon appears → click it → write a description of what you want → Copilot drafts the text into the field.

**Model:** Edge Copilot is powered by GPT-5 (Microsoft's partnership with OpenAI). It uses the page context automatically — you don't need to copy and paste.

## Sider — Multi-Model AI Sidebar for Chrome and Edge

Sider is the most popular third-party AI sidebar extension, with over 4 million installs. It works in both Chrome and Edge.

**Install:** Go to the Chrome Web Store → search "Sider" → Install. It's free with a daily usage limit; the paid plan removes limits.

**What makes Sider different:** You can switch between models — Claude, GPT-5, Gemini — from a single sidebar. If one model gives a poor answer, switch and ask again in one click.

**Key features:**
- **Page chat:** Ask questions about any page you're reading without switching tabs
- **Quick tools:** Select any text → right-click → Sider offers: Explain, Summarize, Translate, Improve Writing, Reply to (for emails/messages)
- **Writing:** Works in Gmail, Outlook Web, LinkedIn, any web text area — click the Sider icon and get a draft
- **YouTube:** On YouTube videos, Sider shows a transcript summary in the sidebar
- **PDF reader:** Open any PDF in the browser → Sider lets you ask questions about it

**Privacy note:** Sider sends selected text and page content to its servers, which then call AI provider APIs. For sensitive content (legal documents, financial records, confidential emails) do not use Sider — use a direct API call or a local model instead.

## Other Notable Extensions

**Monica (Chrome/Edge):** Similar to Sider — multi-model sidebar with free tier. Slightly more focused on writing and content generation. Good alternative if you hit Sider's free limits.

**Merlin (Chrome/Edge):** Free tier with 50 queries/day. Strong for reading and summarizing LinkedIn posts, web articles, and PDFs. Popular with researchers.

**ChatGPT extension (Chrome):** Adds a button to open ChatGPT alongside any search. Primarily useful if you're already in the OpenAI ecosystem.

**Grammarly (Chrome/Edge/Firefox):** Not purely a generalist AI tool, but indispensable for office writing. Checks grammar, tone, and clarity in any web text area — Gmail, Outlook Web, LinkedIn, web forms. The paid tier adds full rewrites and tone adjustment.

**DeepL (Chrome):** Best-in-class AI translation. Select any text on any page → right-click → Translate with DeepL. Far more accurate than Google Translate for most European languages and Japanese.

**Use Edge for sensitive work, Sider for general productivity.** Edge Copilot processes pages on Microsoft's infrastructure (subject to M365 data policies). Sider routes through third-party APIs. For legal documents, financial data, or confidential business content, use Edge Copilot or paste into Claude.ai directly — not a third-party extension.

sections.title: Install and Use a Browser AI Extension
sections.content:
By the end of this workshop, AI will be one right-click away on every webpage you visit.

**Step 1 — Choose and install (5 minutes)**

Pick one:
- **Edge users:** No install needed — press `Ctrl+Shift+.` to open Copilot sidebar now
- **Chrome users:** Go to the Chrome Web Store, search "Sider", click **Add to Chrome**, confirm

**Step 2 — Summarize a long article (5 minutes)**

1. Find a long article — a news story, a blog post, a Wikipedia page, anything with 500+ words
2. Open the AI sidebar (Edge: `Ctrl+Shift+.` / Sider: click the sidebar icon on the right)
3. Ask: *"Summarize this page in 5 bullet points. Include the main argument and any important numbers or dates."*
4. Read the summary — does it capture the article accurately?

**Step 3 — Improve text in a web form (5 minutes)**

1. Open Gmail (mail.google.com) or Outlook Web (outlook.com) and start composing a new message (you can discard it)
2. Type a rough, informal version of what you want to say — don't worry about quality
3. Select all the text you typed
4. In Sider: right-click → Sider → **Improve Writing**. In Edge: Copilot sidebar → type *"Rewrite this as a professional email: [paste your text]"*
5. Review the improved version — does it sound like you but more polished?

**In your notes:** Write one sentence about which AI browser tool you installed and what you'll use it for most often.

sections.question: You're reviewing a 30-page supplier contract in PDF format in your browser. You need to quickly find any clauses about liability and payment terms. What is the most efficient approach using browser AI?
options: Read all 30 pages carefully to ensure you don't miss anything
Open the PDF in your browser with Sider or Edge Copilot active, then ask specific questions about liability and payment terms
Download the PDF, open it in Acrobat, and use Ctrl+F to search for keywords
Email the PDF to your legal team and wait for their review
sections.explanation: Browser AI extensions that support PDF can read the document and answer targeted questions — far faster than reading 30 pages or using keyword search. You ask in plain English what you're looking for, and the AI locates and summarizes the relevant clauses. Keyword search (C) misses paraphrased language. Emailing to legal (D) is appropriate for final review but not for a quick initial scan. Reading all 30 pages (A) is necessary for high-stakes review but not for an initial orientation.

sections.title: Workshop A — Browser AI Extension Quick Test
sections.content:
Install and test a browser AI extension on a real webpage in 8 minutes.

**Step 1 — Install one browser AI extension** if you haven't already. Options:
- Sider (sider.ai) — works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox
- Monica — AI assistant in Chrome
- Merlin — AI on any page
- Or use the native Copilot sidebar in Edge

**Step 2 — Navigate to a webpage you actually read** for work: an industry publication, a long article, a company's product page, documentation.

**Step 3 — Open the AI extension sidebar** and test 3 things:
- "Summarise this page" — how good is the summary?
- Ask a specific question about the page content — does it answer correctly?
- Ask something the page doesn't cover — does it acknowledge it doesn't know, or make something up?

**Step 4 — Test it on a page you know deeply** — something in your area of expertise. Catch any errors in what it tells you.

**Step 5 — Rate the extension:** Is it faster and more useful than copying text into Claude? When would you use each?

sections.title: Workshop B — AI Research Workflow for Industry Reading
sections.content:
Build a browser AI workflow that makes your regular industry reading faster and more useful.

**Step 1 — Identify 3 websites you read regularly** for work: news sites, industry blogs, competitor sites, documentation.

**Step 2 — Open a real article** from one of these sites. Use your browser AI extension to:
- Get a summary
- Extract the 3 most important implications for your specific work
- Identify any claims that seem questionable or that you should verify

**Step 3 — Ask the AI:** *"What questions should I research further based on this article? What context would change how I interpret the main claims?"*

**Step 4 — Mandatory review:** Ask the AI: *"Review your own summary. What important nuance or context from the article did you omit? What might a reader of your summary misunderstand?"* Compare to the original.

**Step 5 — Create a "reading workflow" prompt** you will use every time you read industry content: a standard set of questions that extract the most value from any article for your specific role.

**Step 6 — Save your reading workflow prompt** in your prompt library.

sections.title: Workshop C — Accuracy Test: Browser AI vs Reality
sections.content:
Browser AI extensions read and summarise pages — but how accurate are they?

**Step 1 — Choose an article or page you have already read** and understand well.

**Step 2 — Without telling the AI you know the content**, ask it to summarise the page and answer 3 specific questions about it.

**Step 3 — Evaluate each answer:**
- Is the summary accurate to what was actually said?
- Did it correctly answer the specific questions?
- Did it add anything not in the original (hallucination)?
- Did it miss the most important point?

**Step 4 — Ask the AI to identify the single most controversial or surprising claim in the article.** Was its identification accurate?

**Step 5 — Write your finding:** For this type of content (technical/news/opinion/etc.), how much do you trust the browser AI's analysis without verification?

sections.title: Workshop D — Build Your Browser AI Toolkit
sections.content:
Set up a consistent browser AI workflow you'll actually use every day.

**Step 1 — Choose your browser AI tool.** If you use Edge: built-in Copilot sidebar. If Chrome/Firefox: install one extension (Sider is a solid choice).

**Step 2 — Configure it** with any personalisation options available: preferred AI model, response language, default summarisation style.

**Step 3 — Create a personal quick-prompt menu.** Most extensions let you save custom prompts. Save these:
- "Summarise for someone in [your role]"
- "What are the key implications for [your industry]?"
- "What should I verify before acting on this?"
- "Extract all action items and deadlines mentioned"

**Step 4 — Test your saved prompts** on 3 different pages.

**Step 5 — Set a 2-week commitment:** Use your browser AI extension every time you read a long article for work. After 2 weeks, decide if it's worth keeping.

sections.question: You use a browser AI extension to summarise a complex legal document. The summary looks clean and professional. What should you do before relying on it?
options: Use it directly — browser AI extensions are specifically designed for document analysis
Read the key sections of the original document to verify the summary captured the critical points accurately
Ask the extension to verify its own summary
Use two different extensions and compare summaries
sections.explanation: Browser AI summaries of complex documents (legal, medical, financial, technical) should always be verified against the original for critical decisions. AI excels at making content readable but can miss critical qualifications, conditions, exceptions, or nuances that are legally or practically important. For complex professional documents, the summary is a starting point for reading, not a replacement for it.

sections.question: Which browser AI use case provides the least value and should probably be done another way?
options: Summarising a 5,000-word industry report before deciding whether to read it in full
Translating a webpage from another language
Asking a browser AI to fact-check information it found on the very page you are reading
Extracting a list of key statistics from a research paper
sections.explanation: Asking a browser AI to fact-check using the source it just read is circular — it's verifying claims against the same document that contains those claims. This provides no independent verification. Fact-checking requires an independent source. The other options (summarising before deciding to read, translation, extraction) are all legitimate uses where AI adds genuine value.

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 2-11.** You now have a browser AI extension installed and know how to use it for page summarization, writing improvement, and document Q&A. AI is now available on every page you visit.
